clue.text: Does it set off in pursuit of the sea-hare?

definitions.text: Does it set off in pursuit of the sea-hare?

parts.words: Does it set off in pursuit of the sea-hare?
parts.note: pictures a racing dog chasing a hare across the waves, which is really a fast passenger liner crossing the ocean

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about who chases a sea-hare, the marine slug.
explanation.walkthrough: A greyhound chases a hare; a liner famed for speed on the Atlantic was nicknamed after the racing dog, so the 'sea-hare' it pursues is fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the nickname for a fast transatlantic passenger liner of the steamship era.

clue.text: Where Granny Smith comes from beet is yellow-topped

indicators.note: in a down entry, the beet has the yellow placed on top of it

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
chard is a leaf beet

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a beet plant's leaves have gone yellow at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Granny Smith sounds like a person but is a variety of apple, which grows in fruit-tree plantations.
explanation.definitionFit: A Granny Smith is an apple, and apples are grown in a plantation of fruit trees.

clue.text: Promoters of tuition, as scaled, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the words before it could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: People who push teaching, like those who climbed a ladder of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the fifteen letters of TUITION, AS and SCALED; 'of' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Educational theorists and advocates are people who champion and promote teaching methods.

clue.text: Combed wool of animal on its back

indicators.note: an animal lying on its back is upside down, so in a down entry the word is turned around

parts.note: the lion is an animal

explanation.surface: Wool combed from a beast that is lying belly-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Noil is the short fibre combed out of wool during processing.

clue.text: Escapee loses heart in airstrip

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for the escapee is dropped

parts.note: a runaway is someone who has escaped

explanation.surface: A fugitive loses courage while on an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' suggests discouragement but removes the central A.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip on which aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Desire to be drawing pay after one short year

indicators.note: the earning part comes after the abbreviation for year

parts.note: Y is the short form, an abbreviation, for a single year
earning means drawing pay

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be on a payroll after a year spent without work.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearning is a deep longing or wish for something.

clue.text: Otto Austin coming to grief in distant settlement

indicators.note: coming to grief means being wrecked, so the two names are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man named Otto crashes his Austin car somewhere remote.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin was a British car make, which makes 'coming to grief' read as a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstation is a remote post or settlement far from the main base.

clue.text: He takes care of the pennies (and the pounds, now)

definitions.text: He takes care of the pennies (and the pounds, now)

parts.words: He takes care of the pennies (and the pounds, now)
parts.note: plays on the saying about looking after pennies, meaning a coin specialist, who now also studies pound coins

explanation.surface: A thrifty man who minds his small change and now his larger sums too.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Take care of the pennies and the pounds will take care of themselves' suggests a miser; the pound became a coin in 1983.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin expert studies and collects currency, caring for coins like pennies and pounds.

clue.text: This heavy food makes, for example, spots come up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: dots are spots

explanation.surface: Rich food that brings a teenager out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' reads like spots appearing on skin, but turns the whole run EGDOTS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is thick, starchy, filling food such as suet pudding.

clue.text: Warning! One could be eaten by wild toucan

indicators.note: the numeral is swallowed inside the scrambled bird
wild means out of control, so the bird's letters are scrambled

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A warning that a bird in the wild might eat you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' puts I inside CAUTON, the rearrangement of TOUCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A caution is a warning or admonition.

clue.text: Trial for personal assault!

definitions.meaning: a try or effort at something
as in an ... on someone's life, an attack on a person

explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an effort or try, and an attempt on a life is an attack on someone.

clue.text: First chap to have a mother? No!

definitions.text: First chap to have a mother? No!

parts.words: First chap to have a mother? No!
parts.note: the first man in Genesis had no mother at all, being made from dust

explanation.surface: A question about the first man to have a mother, answered with a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical first man was created, not born, so he was the first man yet had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the first human male, made by God rather than born.

clue.text: Given attractive properties in a bar, perhaps

definitions.text: Given attractive properties in a bar, perhaps

parts.words: Given attractive properties in a bar, perhaps
parts.note: reads like someone made charming in a pub, but means a metal bar given the power to pull iron

explanation.surface: Someone becomes charming over drinks in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; a bar magnet is the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron becomes a magnet when it acquires the power to attract other metal.

clue.text: After caper, I have meat-paste to look forward to

parts.note: an antic is a caper or prank
pâté is a meat paste

explanation.surface: After a frolic, someone looks forward to a snack of pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caper' may suggest the pickled bud eaten with pâté, but it is a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate is to expect or await something eagerly.

clue.text: Stoops like Canute and his followers, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: King Canute and his men were Danes

explanation.surface: King Canute and his men bow down.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute (Cnut) was a Danish king of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, to stoop to doing something beneath one.

clue.text: Get going on coach

definitions.meaning: to instruct someone in the basics or rites

explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is both to begin something and to introduce someone to knowledge, instructing them.

clue.text: State of unused first-class return

parts.note: virgin means unused, untouched

indicators.note: return means the first-class rating comes back the other way

parts.note: A1 means first-class

explanation.surface: A first-class return ticket that has never been used.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of A1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the United States of America.

clue.text: Small metal cup goin 'to pieces, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: going to pieces is panicking, here with a dropped final g as it is said

explanation.surface: A small cup is falling apart, according to people.
explanation.walkthrough: The clipped 'goin'' signals the dropped g, giving 'panickin''.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannikin is a small tin drinking vessel.

clue.text: Flower produced hair-dressing

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Po in Italy
made means produced

explanation.surface: A flower was used to make a hair product.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented ointment for styling hair.

clue.text: Scowl after party — it is the pain

indicators.note: the scowl comes after the party

parts.note: a do is a party
to lour is to scowl or frown

explanation.surface: Someone frowns the morning after a party, nursing a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolour is a literary word for sorrow or grief.

clue.text: Highly esteems goodwill messages

definitions.meaning: good wishes sent to someone, as in 'give her my best'

explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to esteem, and one sends kind regards as good wishes.

clue.text: Doctor normally dressed for battle

annotationWithheld.why: Doctor normally dressed for battle: COMBAT is MB inside COAT, but no clue word gives COAT apart from 'dressed', which would also have to signal the container (two jobs)

clue.text: Becoming softer, get scores in the Crucible

parts.note: melting means becoming softer
to pot is to sink a ball and score in snooker or billiards

explanation.surface: A snooker player loosens up and starts potting balls at the Crucible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible Theatre in Sheffield hosts the World Snooker Championship, so 'get scores' suggests potting.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucible is a vessel in which metals are melted.

clue.text: Medal struck before dinner

definitions.meaning: slang for a decoration or award
a metal disc beaten to summon diners

explanation.definitionFit: Gong is slang for a medal, and a gong is the disc hit to call people to a meal.

clue.text: Quiet demeanour of the couple

parts.note: p (piano) means quiet in music
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: Observing the calm manner of two partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two people or things together.

clue.text: Scorn for platform collapsing in great noise

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the noise

parts.note: din is a great noise

indicators.note: collapsing means the platform falls to bits, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A stage collapses with a loud crash and the audience jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ISDA (the rearrangement of DAIS, from 'collapsing') inside DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is contempt, the feeling that something is beneath one.

clue.text: Brass-worker to carry hot coals

definitions.meaning: a metal pan or stand for holding burning coal

explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is both a worker in brass and a metal stand holding a coal fire.

clue.text: I start to rise, oh, so awkwardly with this condition

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily, so the words before are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone groans as they try to get up with stiff joints.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange I, START, TO, RISE and OH; 'so awkwardly' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a degenerative joint disease, a medical disorder causing stiffness and pain.
